deed: איחוד הצלה שואף להגיע לכל מטופל תוך 90 שניות ומטפל בכל אדם בחינם
title: Eli Beer founded United Hatzalah: volunteers on motorcycles who arrive within minutes and treat for free

trailer.text: Eli Beer was born in Israel to American parents, and according to the organization's website he is the founder of United Hatzalah, Israel's largest independent volunteer emergency medical service.
According to him, at 16 he was on an ambulance that drove for 21 minutes until it reached a seven-year-old boy choking on a hotdog.
According to the organization's website, in 2006 Beer united local Hatzalah groups into one national organization, based on the Jewish value of the sanctity of life.
The dispatch system sends out the volunteers closest to the incident, some of them on a motorcycle with medical equipment, and the goal is to arrive within 90 seconds.
According to the organization, emergency response is provided free of charge to all residents of Israel: Jews, Christians, Muslims and Druze.

stations.title: A choking boy and an ambulance stuck in traffic

paragraphs.text: According to the organization's website, Beer witnessed his first terror attack when he was still a child.
According to Algemeiner, he saw a bus explode in a terrorist attack in his neighborhood in Jerusalem.
Beer said that at 16 he was on an ambulance on a call for a seven-year-old boy choking on a hotdog.
According to Ashoka, the ambulance was delayed because of traffic congestion.
Beer said that a doctor lived only two blocks from the boy, but no one called him.
According to Ashoka, traffic congestion in Israel makes it nearly impossible for an emergency vehicle to travel quickly.
Also according to Ashoka, Israel has no centralized emergency call system.
According to the organization's website, Beer is one of the 15 founders of "Hatzalah Jerusalem", which was later renamed "Hatzalah Israel".
Beer said that it all started with 15 volunteers and one idea: to respond to emergency calls.
Beer said that he bought police scanners to hear emergency calls, without permission.
According to him, when they proposed to Magen David Adom that it share the calls, the workers' union adamantly refused and threw them out of the room.
Moshe Teitelbaum, who was then the organization's director general, told Channel 7 that during the Second Lebanon War, in 2006, there were about 300 rescue volunteers in the country.
According to him, Beer saw that they did not know one another, and asked why they should not unite into one group.
According to the organization's website, in 2006 Beer founded United Hatzalah by uniting local groups.

stations.title: The call, the nearest volunteer and the motorcycle

paragraphs.text: According to the organization's website, as soon as a call comes in, the dispatch system identifies the closest volunteers and dispatches them.
Everyone who is dispatched is a volunteer who receives no payment for it.

According to the organization's website, Beer introduced the "ambucycle", a motorcycle fitted with medical equipment, which volunteers dispersed throughout the country can also use for their daily needs.
According to Teitelbaum, the motorcycles are intended mainly for cities with traffic problems.
According to Teitelbaum, the responders take a six-month course, twice a week, in the evenings.
According to the organization's website, the organization is registered and certified by the Ministry of Health as an emergency medical response agency.
Also according to the website, Beer founded a Psychotrauma Unit, which provides immediate psychological support after traumatic incidents.
According to the organization's website, the goal is to reach every patient within 90 seconds when every moment matters: in a heart attack, stroke, anaphylactic shock, choking or bleeding.
Beer told the Jewish Press that he wants a 90-second response everywhere in Israel.
According to the Jewish Link, this is also why his official biography is called "90 Seconds".
According to the organization's About page, it responds to 2,000 medical emergencies a day, often arriving within minutes, with a goal of 90 seconds.
According to Ashoka, response times fell below three minutes, and in major cities went as low as 90 seconds.
Volunteer Noam Lifshin said that he arrived within a minute and a half to a man who had collapsed in Moshav Regba, and found him without a pulse and without breathing.
Organization spokesperson Raphael Poch told JNS that on a call in Efrat he and another volunteer were alone at the scene for about 40 minutes, until an ambulance arrived.
According to the organization's website, United Hatzalah provides emergency medical care to every person in Israel, free of charge.
According to Teitelbaum, the organization's volunteers are secular, Haredi, religious, Arab and Druze, and they work together.
According to him, at the beginning, volunteering by women was not accepted in the Haredi community.
In an interview in which he spoke about the organization's budget for 2017, Teitelbaum said that the cost of each volunteer is tens of thousands of shekels a year.

According to the organization's website, in 2023 the organization recorded $144 million (533 million ILS) in support, of which $2.6 million (9.5 million ILS) came from the government and the authorities.

According to the organization's website, which relies on Charity Navigator and on Form 990 filings submitted by Friends of United Hatzalah through the end of 2024, over 85% of the spending of Friends of United Hatzalah over the past three years went to lifesaving operations.

stations.title: October 7, and disasters around the world

paragraphs.text: According to the organization's website, on October 7 more than 1,500 volunteers left their families and rushed to the areas under attack.
Official protocols restricted entry into certain locations, yet the volunteers went in to save lives.
According to the website, on that day and in the days that followed, the volunteers treated more than 3,000 victims.
Two volunteers were killed while treating the wounded.
According to the organization's website, volunteer teams also went to disasters abroad: to the war in Ukraine, the earthquakes in Turkey and Morocco, Nepal and Puerto Rico.
Beer told Algemeiner that in Turkey the volunteers were threatened by frustrated residents whose relatives were still missing.
According to the organization's website, Beer has received numerous awards, including Social Entrepreneur of the Year in Israel and the President's Prize from President Shimon Peres.
According to the Jewish Press, he was also selected as a Young Global Leader of the World Economic Forum.
According to Ashoka, in 2013 Beer was elected an Ashoka Fellow.
According to the Genesis Prize Foundation, Beer has spoken at the World Economic Forum in Davos.
The foundation presents him as the founder and president of what it calls the world's largest fully volunteer emergency medical service.
According to the organization's website, the SFI Group has given the organization its Midot Seal of Effectiveness in each of the last three years.
According to Algemeiner, in March 2020 Beer fell ill with coronavirus, and at one point his life was in danger.
According to the organization's website, the CEO today is Prof. Ehud Davidson.

stations.title: What has not yet been achieved

paragraphs.text: The organization writes on its website that it has not yet reached 90 seconds everywhere, and that in some areas it is near the goal.
According to it, response time depends on location, traffic, the number of volunteers near the patient and the type of emergency.
According to Ashoka, Magen David Adom is available in most cities, but gaps in service remain in rural areas.
According to the organization's website, when Beer united the Hatzalah groups in 2006, some of them chose not to join.
United Hatzalah asked the government to allow full and immediate sharing of all emergency calls among all lifesaving organizations.
The organization also proposed a law for a single national emergency number, like 911 in the United States.
According to the website, United Hatzalah and Magen David Adom are generally complementary.

disagreements.question: How long did it take the ambulance to reach the choking boy?

versions.says: Beer, in an interview with the Jewish Press: 21 minutes
Ashoka, in an article on Beer's journey: over twenty minutes
Ashoka, in Beer's profile: more than half an hour

disagreements.question: Did Beer know the American "Hatzalah" model?

versions.says: Beer, to the Jewish Press: he did not know of it and had no connection to it when he founded the organization
Ashoka: Beer had heard of the "Hatzalah" model that started among Hasidic communities in Brooklyn in the 1960s
The organization's website: the organization was built on the well-known "Hatzalah" model from Jewish communities around the world

disagreements.question: How many calls does the organization respond to?

versions.says: The organization's About page: 2,000 emergencies per day

According to the organization's website, United Hatzalah receives an average of 14,400 emergency calls per week across Israel (about 2,000 a day), not including periods in which the number of calls rose because of the war in Gaza.

unknowns.text: The pages do not say in what share of calls the volunteers actually arrive within 90 seconds

Beer said that at 16 he was on an ambulance going to a call for a seven-year-old boy choking on a hotdog, that it took them 21 minutes to arrive, and that a doctor who lived nearby examined the boy and asked for a sheet to cover him, because there was nothing more to be done.
According to the organization's website, two United Hatzalah volunteers, Awad Darawshe and Dolev Yehud, were killed on October 7 while treating victims.

According to the organization's website, United Hatzalah asked the Government of Israel to allow immediate and full sharing of all emergency calls, and it was not stated whether the request was accepted; the organization also proposed legislation to create a single national emergency number, and according to the website such a unified system has not yet been established.

claims.quote: 2 United Hatzalah volunteers were killed while treating victims

claims.text: לפי אתר הארגון, איחוד הצלה שלח צוותי מתנדבים לחו"ל באסונות גדולים, ובהם המלחמה באוקראינה, רעידות האדמה בטורקיה ובמרוקו ואסונות בנפאל ובפוארטו ריקו.
claims.quote: it has sent volunteer teams abroad during major crises, including the war in Ukraine, the earthquakes in Turkey and Morocco, and disasters in Nepal and Puerto Rico

claims.text: לפי Algemeiner ב-2023, מתנדבי הארגון היו לאחרונה בטורקיה לסייע אחרי רעידת האדמה של החודש הקודם.
claims.quote: they were most recently in Turkey to help in the aftermath of last month’s deadly earthquake

claims.text: לפי ביר, מתנדבי איחוד הצלה בטורקיה התמודדו עם איומי ביטחון מצד תושבים מתוסכלים שקרוביהם נותרו נעדרים.
claims.quote: United Hatzalah volunteers also faced security threats from residents who were getting frustrated as their family members remained missing.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, ביר קיבל פרסים רבים, ובהם מנהיג גלובלי צעיר של הפורום הכלכלי העולמי ופרס הנשיא להתנדבות בישראל.
claims.quote: Beer’s dedication to saving lives has earned him numerous awards, including the World Economic Forum’s Young Global Leaders in Davos, the Presidential Award for Volunteerism in Israel

claims.text: לפי אשוקה, אלי ביר נבחר ב-2013 לעמית אשוקה והקים רשת מתנדבים רפואיים שממלאת את הפער בין הקריאה לבין הגעת אנשי המקצוע.
claims.quote: As a social entrepreneur, Eli Beer (Ashoka Fellow, elected in 2013) has created a strong network of volunteer emergency medical helpers

claims.text: לפי קרן פרס ג'נסיס, ביר נאם בפורום הכלכלי העולמי בדאבוס וקיבל פרסים רבים על שירות הומניטרי.
claims.quote: He has spoken at the World Economic Forum in Davos and received numerous awards for humanitarian service

claims.text: לפי קרן פרס ג'נסיס, אלי ביר הוא מייסד ונשיא איחוד הצלה ישראל, שירות הרפואה החירום ההתנדבותי הגדול בעולם.
claims.quote: Eli Beer is the visionary founder and president of United Hatzalah of Israel, the world’s largest fully volunteer emergency medical service.

claims.text: לפי אתר הארגון, קבוצת SFI העניקה לאיחוד הצלה את חותם מידות להצלחה בכל אחת משלוש השנים האחרונות.
claims.quote: has given UH its Midot Seal of Effectiveness each of the last three years

claims.text: לפי Algemeiner, ביר חלה בקורונה במרץ 2020 ועבר חוויה של סכנת חיים.
claims.quote: The father-of-five had his own near-death experience in March 2020 when he was diagnosed with coronavirus

claims.text: לפי אתר הארגון, מנכ"ל איחוד הצלה ישראל הוא פרופ' אהוד דוידסון.
claims.quote: The CEO of United Hatzalah Israel is Prof. Ehud Davidson.

claims.text: הארגון מודה באתר שלו שהוא עדיין לא השיג זמן תגובה של 90 שניות בכל מקום, ושיש אזורים שבהם הוא קרוב ליעד.
claims.quote: There are some areas where we are near to achieving our goal of consistent 90 second response time coverage.

claims.text: לפי אתר הארגון, זמני התגובה בפועל משתנים לפי מיקום, תנועה, צפיפות המתנדבים ליד המטופל וסוג החירום.
claims.quote: Actual response times vary depending on location, traffic, density of a volunteer(s) near the patient and the type of emergency.

claims.text: לפי אשוקה, מגן דוד אדום זמין ברוב האזורים העירוניים, אך הדבר משאיר פערי שירות באזורים כפריים.
claims.quote: Magen David Adom, the Israeli equivalent of the Red Cross, is available in most urban areas to send ambulances to accident victims, but that leaves gaps in service in rural areas.

claims.text: לפי אתר הארגון, איחוד הצלה ביקש מממשלת ישראל לאפשר שיתוף מיידי ומלא של כל קריאת חירום בין כל ארגוני ההצלה.
claims.quote: United Hatzalah has requested that the Government of Israel allow every emergency call to be immediately and fully shared among every life-saving organization

claims.text: לפי אתר הארגון, איחוד הצלה הציע חקיקה להקמת מספר חירום ארצי יחיד, בדומה ל-911 בארה"ב.
claims.quote: United Hatzalah has proposed legislation to create a single national emergency number, similar to 911 in the United States

claims.text: לפי אתר הארגון, איחוד הצלה ומד"א משלימים זה את זה בדרך כלל, ואיחוד הצלה מנצל את רשת המתנדבים, הצי והטכנולוגיה כדי להגיע ראשון לאירועים.
claims.quote: The two organizations are generally complementary, as UH leverages its volunteer network, its fleet of vehicles and its proprietary technology to arrive at emergencies first.

claims.text: לפי פרופיל אשוקה, צוות האמבולנס של ביר לקח יותר ממחצית השעה להגיע לילד שנחנק.
claims.quote: While on duty, Eli’s ambulance team took more than half an hour to get to a choking child.

claims.text: ביר סיפר שלא הכיר את "הצלה" באמריקה ולא היה לו קשר אליה כשהקים את הארגון.
claims.quote: No. There was no Internet then, and I didn’t know of or have any connection to Hatzalah in America.

claims.text: לפי אשוקה, ביר שמע על מודל "הצלה" שהחל בקהילות חסידיות בברוקלין בשנות ה-60.
claims.quote: Eli had heard of the Hatzalah model that started among Hasidic communities in Brooklyn in the 1960s

claims.text: לפי אתר הארגון, איחוד הצלה מקבל בממוצע 14,400 קריאות חירום בשבוע ברחבי ישראל, לא כולל תקופות שבהן עלה מספר הקריאות בשל המלחמה בעזה.
claims.quote: United Hatzalah receives an average of 14,400 emergency calls per week across Israel.

claims.text: אלי ביר נולד בישראל להורים אמריקנים, ולפי אתר הארגון הוא מייסד איחוד הצלה, שירות הרפואה החירום ההתנדבותי העצמאי הגדול בישראל.
claims.quote: United Hatzalah is Israel’s largest independent, non-profit volunteer emergency medical service
claims.checker_note: audit: page could not be fetched by script; verifier quoted it

claims.text: משה טייטלבאום, שהיה אז מנכ"ל הארגון, סיפר לערוץ 7 שבמלחמת לבנון השנייה, ב-2006, היו בארץ כ-300 מתנדבי הצלה.
claims.quote: מנכ"ל הארגון בשלוש השנים האחרונות
claims.checker_note: audit: quote found on the fetched page

quote_translations.c52: In the Second Lebanon War, in 2006, there were about 300 Hatzalah volunteers throughout the country.
quote_translations.c53: Eli Beer, the organization's president, saw that no one knew the other and wondered why not unite and form one group
quote_translations.c58: We direct the motorcycles mainly to cities that have traffic problems.
quote_translations.c56: There is of course the training of the responders, who take a six-month course twice a week in an evening track.
quote_translations.c63: I got there within a minute and a half and saw a person lying on the floor without a pulse and breathing
quote_translations.c54: Because today we have volunteers who are secular, Haredi, religious, Arab, Druze
quote_translations.c55: At the beginning there was a problem with women, it was not accepted in the Haredi community.
quote_translations.c61: The cost of each volunteer is tens of thousands of shekels a year.
